items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I was with George E. Lee in '29 and '30

ctx.x: And I ran into him when I was with George E. Lee, because I haven't got to when I joined George E. Lee, back in Oklahoma, and Ben came up to where I was working to show me how great he could play the saxophone, and this cat like to blew me off the stand.
And so finally Ben came back to Kansas City.

items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: And from then on we became good friends.

ctx.x: I couldn't believe it. I said, what? So after he played all his horn, he came back down to the bar, and he said, Budd Johnson, you don't remember me, he says, you couldn't remember me because I was just a little cat; when you was around Kansas City, I was the little cat out front playing stick ball on Euclid Avenue in front of George E. Georgia Lee's mother's house where you guys used to rehearse, and I would peep through the window listening to you guys. And Charlie Parker couldn't have been over ten or 11 years…
And from then on we became good friends.
